title: The keys
logline: The uncle's hand with the shack's keys, the day the mill closed. The whistle drawn as a shape over the stack. The sentence the sequence is built around, in a caption, once.

panels.composition: Close: a weathered hand holding two keys on a ring of frayed cord — the shack's keys, the dock gate's. Behind and above, out of focus, the stack, and over it the mill whistle drawn as a jagged shape, the last one. The hand is the whole foreground. One caption, small, at the bottom.
panels.caption: He said: well, there's the shack.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a close view of a weathered older man's hand holding two keys on a frayed cord ring, a tall smokestack out of focus behind with a jagged sound shape drawn above it, heavy black spotting, no words
image.notes: Letter after. The one sentence of the sequence.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run

notes: 'Well, there's the shack.' The keys. The whistle.
